# \#proprioception (2)
## 1
> [!info]+ 1
> Anxiety manifests biologically through altered somatosensory cortex activity, particularly in the right postcentral gyrus, which directly processes bodily sensations ([[Why Anxiety?#Somatosensory Cortices]], #cognitive/anxiety/state_anxiety/bio/somatosensory_cortex). The somatosensory cortex participates in emotional regulation and exhibits structural and functional changes in anxiety disorders ([[Target word 'somatosensory_cortex and anxiety or proprioception']], Higher-Order Roles Perception Emotion Social, #cognitive/anxiety/trait_anxiety, #somatosensory_cortex/emotional_regulation). This neural architecture creates a direct pathway through which anxiety disrupts the proprioceptive feedback essential for wearable robot control—proprioception being the sensory modality most affected by wearable robots and carrying the most weight in system performance ([[Why Anxiety?#^9b4e49]], #proprioception). ^tr-4z9f7llbo
>

# \#perception/safety/factors/human_factors/sense_of_ownership (1)
## 1
> [!info]+ 1
> This is catastrophic for wearable robots because proprioception acts as the sensory mediator for the "Sense of Agency"—without precise proprioceptive feedback, the user cannot achieve the psychological state of "human-in-the-loop" trust ([[Why Anxiety?#Embodiment and Proprioception]]). Proprioception is richly represented in the somatosensory cortex, especially S1, where it is integrated with touch and used to update internal body representations (Why Anxiety?, [[Somatosensory Cortices]], #somatosensory_cortex). When anxiety disrupts this integration, embodiment—the sense of ownership and agency critical for natural movement, intuitive control, and effective rehabilitation—becomes impossible (Target word 'cognitive or perception', 1 Embodiment Drives Functional Success, #perception/safety/factors/human_factors/sense_of_agency, #perception/safety/factors/human_factors/sense_of_ownership). ^tr-r3ipyd9pr

> [!info]+ 2
> - S1 and S2 process **tactile, pressure, thermal, and nociceptive (pain)** inputs from skin, muscles, and joints ([[#^a3580e|Xu et al., 2025]]; [[#^102f57|Kropf et al., 2018]]; [[#^9814ca|Lamorie-Foote et al., 2024]]). #somatosensory_cortex^so
> - S1 is especially important for **fine discrimination** of mechanical and cooling stimuli and setting sensory thresholds ([[#^a3580e|Xu et al., 2025]]; [[#^9c8180|Ziegler et al., 2023]]; [[#^0826cf|Taub et al., 2024]]; [[#^e92f97|Liang et al., 2011]]). #somatosensory_cortex/s1 #Sensory_Processing 
> - S1 is the "first stop" for sensory signals (touch, pain, temperature) coming from the thalamus [Ch5, Somatosensory Processes](https://nba.uth.tmc.edu/neuroscience/m/s2/chapter05.html) #Sensory_Processing  #somatosensory_cortex/s1 #somatosensory_cortex 
> - S2 contributes strongly to **mechanical and heat sensitivity** and helps set basal sensory thresholds via its outputs to secondary motor cortex (M2) ([[#^0826cf|Taub et al., 2024]]; [[#^8b1e1d|Taub et al., 2022]]). #motor_control/motor_cortex/M2 #somatosensory_cortex/s2 #Sensory_Processing

# \#somatosensory_cortex (3)
## 1
> [!info]+ 1
> > The **somatosensory** nervous system maintains the sensation within the various dermatomes of sensation throughout the body. 
> > The somatosensory pathway is the conduit between the different sensory modalities **within the body**, sending information from the periphery to the **postcentral gyrus** and associated cortices to convey information from the surrounding environment. #somatosensory_cortex/postcentral_gyrus 
> > Peripheral mechanoreceptors, chemoreceptors, thermoreceptors, and nociceptors transmit information via specific nerve fibers that enter the central nervous system tracts towards the brain. 
> > Each carrying a unique modality of sensation, these senses are ultimately processed and integrated into the central nervous system to help individuals interact with their environmental stimuli. 
> > *The ultimate destination of these sensory stimuli is the somatosensory cortex.* #somatosensory_cortex #somatosensory_cortex/mechanoreceptors #somatosensory_cortex/chemoreceptors #somatosensory_cortex/thermoseptore #somatosensory_cortex/noiceptors #Sensory_Processing ^tr-vn39txcvf

# \#somatosensory_cortex/somatic_dimention_of_empathy (1)
## 1
> [!info]+ 1
> - S2 encodes a continuum from **pure sensory** to **perceptual/choice-related** activity, linking touch to decisions and categories ([[#^f677b0|Condylis et al., 2020]]; [[#^2ad429|Rossi-Pool et al., 2021]] ).
> - Somatosensory cortex supports **body perception, [[Body Ownership]], haptic object recognition, and action guidance** ([[#^9837aa|De Haan & Dijkerman, 2020]]). #somatosensory_cortex/body_perception #perception/proprioception #somatosensory_cortex/sense_of_ownership #somatosensory_cortex/haptic_object_recognition #somatosensory_cortex/action_guidance

> - During social perception, somatosensory cortices are vicariously activated when seeing others’ touch or pain, adding a **somatic dimension to empathy** ([[#^928df3|Keysers et al., 2010]]). #somatosensory_cortex/somatic_dimention_of_empathy ^tr-p7zpusl9v
